answer: Agents can require each new identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake in a shared vault, then earn influence only through work that independent peers verify over time. A nebula of cheap accounts therefore cannot gain voting weight merely by multiplying names: each account needs capital at risk, and proven fraud lets the system slash its stake. A raven attacker must fund every Sybil and risks losing those deposits, making an attack costly rather than free.
